library.description: Runtime-neutral storage host and typed backend authoring

blocks.text: 把内存、数据库和文件后端装到同一个存储宿主（host），用带类型的 `backend(id)` 获取对应存储，并统一结束工作与释放资源。适合同时使用多个数据源、需要组织隔离或事务的应用：先安装后端插件，再选择各后端提供的能力；多个后端的写入不会自动合成一个原子事务。
English · 使用指南

items: 数据库连接关了，订阅或排队任务还在运行：业务代码没有统一的结束入口。
两个后端都叫 `cache`，调用时才发现拿错实例：字符串查找丢失了安装时的类型信息。
给每个方法手动加租户前缀，偶尔漏掉一次：组织隔离依赖调用方逐项遵守约定。
同时更新文本和记录，一半成功一半失败：多次独立写入没有放进同一个事务。
`backend(id)` 保留已安装插件的具体类型；重复 ID 在安装时拒绝。安装后端
内置 memory 后端可直接存文本、字节和记录，也能执行事务。事务与查询
`org(id)` 固定同一组织，传递给实体或组合插件后仍保持隔离。组织数据
`dispose()` 等待已接纳的工作并释放已安装资源；组织视图没有关闭整个宿主的方法。结束工作

items: `plugins` 的 ID 必须唯一。一批插件全部成功才会出现在查找结果中；安装失败会释放本批已创建的资源。重叠安装批次报 `STORAGE_HOST_BUSY`。
`autoDetect` 默认 `true`，`installTimeoutMs` 默认 `30000` 毫秒。设 `autoDetect: false` 后，应先 `await host.detect()` 再执行数据操作；检查未完成的操作会报 `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`。追加插件后也要检查新增后端。
`org` 默认零 UUID；显式组织 ID 必须是规范的小写 UUID，可用 `createOrgId()` 生成。`org()` 返回的视图不能安装插件、删除组织或关闭宿主。删除组织尝试所有后端，部分失败不会撤回已成功的删除，错误为 `ORG_DELETE_FAILED`，具体失败在 `AggregateError.errors` 中。
后端支持什么能力由实际实例决定。非默认组织不会自动得到只绑定到根后端的自定义能力；先检查 `has(token)`。组织视图不支持原生 SQL/SPARQL 入口。
显式 `dispose()` 的失败会拒绝，重复调用复用同一个 Promise。`await using` 清理会报告失败并完成，以免覆盖业务代码的主错误。调用方提供的原生客户端是否需要单独关闭，见相应后端说明。
宿主错误的 `source` 为 `@migaia/storage-host`；共享参数和能力错误来自 `@migaia/storage-contract`。排查时同时读取 `source`、`code` 与 `cause`，不要匹配错误文案。

blocks.text: 应用只调用 `backend()` 时无需导入作者工具。实现后端时，运行时工具从以下入口获取；类型、能力 token、定义和纯校验继续从 contract 获取。
表中的 `/authoring/...` 均以 `@migaia/storage-host` 开头。

blocks.text: 完整路径和依赖说明见 storage-contract。旧 contract 根入口不保留这些运行时导出。
实体装配变更：`/entity` 提供基础读写。旧版自动包含的查询、索引、unique 检查、迁移和 keyset，现需在 `features` 中声明对应 `/entity/*` 单元；业务只导入需要的单元。缺少时抛出 `ENTITY_FEATURE_REQUIRED`。迁移方式见实体仓储。
基础宿主不导入 journal runtime、通知控制器或变更迭代器。此前 journal 选项会自动加载日志实现，memory 默认提供变更通知和 watch；现在这些能力由业务显式选择，避免基础存读包含未使用代码。
使用 journal 选项或 `storageLogStore()` 前，在同一插件列表中把从 `@migaia/storage-host/journal` 导入的 `storageJournalPlugin()` 放到后端前。缺少插件时报 `JOURNAL_NOT_ASSEMBLED`。配置格式、日志内容和事务提交语义保持原契约。
memory 通知和变更流分别由两个 Feature 装配：

未选择变更流时，memory 的 `capabilities.changeFeed` 为 `false`；调用 watch 报 `CHANGE_ITERATOR_NOT_ASSEMBLED`。只选通知可调用 `subscribeChanges()`；变更流依赖通知，缺少通知时报 `CHANGE_CONTROLLER_NOT_ASSEMBLED`。基础读写与物理资源关闭仍由轻量生命周期 owner 负责。

后端作者从 `/authoring/change-controller` 导入通知工厂，并显式传给 `core.createChangeController(options, createBackendChangeController)`。基础物理资源可使用同入口的 `createBackendLifecycleController`。变更迭代器改从 `/authoring/change-iterator` 导入，不再从 `/authoring/backend` 转出。
English · 概览与安装

blocks.text: 初始插件放在 `plugins` 数组中。后续 `use()` 返回带新增后端类型的宿主；两者共享同一个生命周期，关闭其中一个宿主引用一次即可。
同一批次里的插件不能借用彼此尚未发布的后端。缓存、归档等组合插件需要读取已有后端时，应先完成基础后端安装，再 `use()` 安装组合插件。ID 必须在整个宿主中唯一。
`autoDetect` 默认开启。需要先完成配置再检查环境时，可设置 `autoDetect: false`，随后显式 `detect()`。并发检查共享同一个 Promise；成功结果会缓存，失败后可再次调用。`installTimeoutMs` 是整批安装的毫秒上限，默认 `30000`，允许有限非负数。安装失败会回滚本批资源，不删除早先已成功安装的后端。
memory 的文本、字节和记录可以在同一个事务中写入。回调失败时草稿不提交。查询从 `records` 能力取得，下面在事务结束后读取已提交记录。
memory 的记录过滤在客户端执行。换用数据库后端时，下推能力和事务范围由该后端决定。事务可能因冲突重放回调；不要在回调中发送邮件、扣款或执行其它无法随事务回滚的副作用。
同一逻辑键的文本、字节和记录有通道冲突规则。需要替换已有通道时，应明确选择相应写入策略，不把三种值当成互不相干的键空间。批量写入的重复键会在提交前拒绝；批量删除的重复键只计一次。
`/entity` 现在只包含定义、连接和基础读写。附加能力需从独立子路径显式装配；缺少装配时抛出 `source: @migaia/storage-host`、`code: ENTITY_FEATURE_REQUIRED`，消息写明所需导入。

只在 `features` 中选择用到的单元：`/entity/query` 的 `entityQueryFeature()` 开启 query/list/stream；`/entity/indexes` 的 `entityIndexesFeature()` 开启索引声明和规划；`/entity/unique` 的 `entityUniqueFeature()` 开启唯一提交检查；`/entity/migration` 的 `entityMigrationFeature()` 开启版本计划和持久迁移；`/entity/keyset` 的 `entityKeysetFeature()` 准入 page/after。索引查询与唯一约束的回退校验还需要 query。没有索引或唯一约束的迁移直接扫描原生记录或文本键，不需要 query 或 unique。单元不会自动开启其他单元。
unique 单元能单独捕获约束投影，不会因此开启索引规划；仅做唯一写入检查时不需 indexes 单元。
`defineEntity<T>()({...})` 声明对象的主键与索引，`connect(store)` 连接实际后端。下面先写入，再用同一声明查询。
实体不会关闭传入的后端。事务中使用 `orders.in(tx)`；`orders.batch(...)` 使用一个原生记录事务。schema 与 codec 用于运行时校验和转换，TypeScript 类型本身不校验外部输入。需要外部 schema 时，可从同一 `/entity` 入口使用 `fromStandardSchema`；转换失败保留原错误在 `cause` 中。

查询的 `index` 或 `range` 要最先选择，且只能选一次；普通 `where`、`select`、`skip`、`limit` 会产生新分支。自定义比较器应搭配有限 `limit`，或使用 `first()`。`stream()` 返回可释放迭代器；提前停止时使用 `await using` 或显式 `dispose()`。`watch()` 是可用后端的失效通知，并非结果行流，也不保证重放。事务查询没有 `watch()`。
迁移没有索引或唯一约束的记录时，只需选择 migration 单元。读取旧记录会升级返回值；需要持久化新版本信封时，再调用 `migrate()`。内存记录的每个迁移批次沿用原生事务。
声明唯一约束时仍需选择 unique 单元；其回退校验还需要 query。迁移不会隐式补装任何一个单元。
组织 ID 是规范小写 UUID。保存组织视图后，同一视图的提取方法也继续使用该组织。
省略 `org` 选项时，根后端使用零 UUID。memory 的每个插件实例独立，namespace 相同也不会共享数据。组织视图只提供业务操作，没有安装与关闭方法。`dropOrg()` 尝试所有后端；一个失败不撤回其它成功删除，调用方应检查聚合错误。不要把多后端组织删除视为一个全局事务。
非默认组织只获得其后端实际提供的能力。根后端上的自定义 capability 不会自动复制；Feature 的 `api` 方法则经组织视图调用。原生 SQL/SPARQL 不支持组织视图，应使用对应组织化数据接口。
先安装可选 peer `@migaia/logger`。`storageLogStore()` 是异步工厂，接受宿主或组织视图、后端 ID 和非空 `prefix`，不能传普通 KV 对象。下面追加一条记录，再读取序号与待处理状态。
日志记录与业务键分开；业务枚举、clear 和容量限制不会操作日志。后端必须支持所需日志存储，打开时先恢复已确认状态。独占存储上的同一组织与前缀只允许一个打开句柄；支持共享事务的存储可允许多个句柄。序号不因截断而重用。写入是否提交无法确认时，日志停止接纳操作，应关闭后重新打开恢复。`dropOrg()` 后旧日志句柄报 `STORE_DISPOSED`。

打开日志不等于开启自动业务日志。自动记录需要 `createStorageHost({ plugins: [storageJournalPlugin(), backend], journal: ... })`；配置可以直接提供 `{ logger, namespace, ... }`，或用异步初始化函数为每个组织准备配置。初始化函数接收 `orgId` 和异步 `storageLogStore(id, { prefix })`。宿主借用 logger，不负责 shutdown。

根据需要选择 binlog、WAL、undo 与同事务日志对象。`atomicBinlog` / `atomicUndo` 按后端 ID 指定真实日志存储；需要它们与业务后端能在同一事务提交。其它组合是否可用由实际后端支持决定，不支持会在业务修改前拒绝。外置 binlog 追加失败会报告，已提交业务数据不回滚；结果未知不能通过盲目重放写入恢复。undo 先检查记录与修订，冲突为 `UNDO_CONFLICT`，缺失为 `UNDO_NOT_FOUND`。

开启 `telemetry: true` 还需要 logger 的 level 插件；日志可能包含操作 payload 和错误，应按应用要求配置 logger。只开 telemetry 也会安装异步阶段，此时使用异步数据方法；同步读写会报 `ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY`。没有配置 journal 且没有导入 `/journal` 时，宿主运行时不加载 logger。更多 logger 配置见 logger 指南。
业务失败会通过调用的 Promise 返回；观察监听器和报告回调的失败不改变已完成的数据操作。配置 `report(error)` 接收这类诊断，检查 `source`、`code` 和原始 `cause`。

Bring memory, database and file backends into one storage host, select each through typed `backend(id)` calls, and finish storage work with one cleanup entry point. Use it when an application needs several data sources, organization isolation or transactions: install the relevant plugins, then select the capabilities each backend provides. Writes across separate backends do not automatically form one atomic transaction.
中文 · Usage guide

items: A database connection closes while subscriptions or queued work are still running: there is no shared shutdown point.
Two instances both use the name `cache`, and a string lookup finds the wrong one: installation types were lost.
A missed tenant prefix exposes another organization's key: isolation depends on every caller remembering the convention.
Updating a string and a record leaves only one write committed: separate calls were used instead of a transaction.
`backend(id)` retains the installed plugin's concrete type. Duplicate IDs are rejected during installation. Install backends
The included memory backend stores strings, bytes and records, with transactions across those channels. Transactions
`org(id)` keeps one organization fixed when passed to entities or composed plugins. Organization data
`dispose()` waits for work already started and releases installed resources. Organization views cannot close the whole host. Shutdown

items: Plugin IDs must be unique. A batch becomes visible only after every installation succeeds; failed installation releases resources created by that batch. Overlapping batches reject with `STORAGE_HOST_BUSY`.

`autoDetect` defaults to `true`; `installTimeoutMs` defaults to `30000`. With `autoDetect: false`, call `await host.detect()` before data operations. Operations whose checks are unfinished reject with `UNSUPPORTED_CAPABILITY`. Check newly added backends after `use()` as well.

The default `org` is the zero UUID. Explicit IDs must be canonical lowercase UUIDs; `createOrgId()` generates one. An organization view cannot install plugins, drop organizations or close the host. `dropOrg()` attempts every backend; successful deletions remain if another fails. `ORG_DELETE_FAILED` exposes the failures through `AggregateError.errors`.

Capabilities depend on the actual backend instance. A non-default organization does not automatically inherit a custom capability attached only to the root backend; check `has(token)`. Native SQL/SPARQL entry points are unavailable through organization views.

Explicit `dispose()` rejects on cleanup failure and reuses its Promise on repeated calls. `await using` cleanup reports failures and completes so it does not replace a primary business error. See each backend's guide for closing caller-supplied native clients.

Host errors use `source: '@migaia/storage-host'`. Shared argument and capability errors come from `@migaia/storage-contract`. Inspect `source`, `code` and `cause` together rather than matching message text.

blocks.text: Applications that only call `backend()` do not need authoring tools. Backend implementations now import runtime tools from these entries; types, capability tokens, definitions and pure validators remain in contract.
Paths beginning `/authoring/...` below are prefixed with `@migaia/storage-host`.

rows: Key encoding, input snapshots and resources

blocks.text: See storage-contract for full paths and dependencies. The old contract root no longer exports these runtime tools.

Entity assembly changes: `/entity` provides basic reads/writes. Previously automatic query, indexes, unique checks, migration and keyset now require their own `/entity/*` units in `features`. Import only the units used by the application; missing units throw `ENTITY_FEATURE_REQUIRED`. See entity setup.

The base host does not import journal runtime, notification controllers or change iterators. Previously journal options loaded logging automatically and memory enabled notifications and watch by default. Applications now select these capabilities so basic reads and writes do not include unused code.

Before using journal options or `storageLogStore()`, import `storageJournalPlugin()` from `@migaia/storage-host/journal` and place it before the backend in the same plugin list. Missing assembly raises `JOURNAL_NOT_ASSEMBLED`. Journal configuration, stored records and transaction semantics retain their existing contract.
Memory notifications and feeds use separate Feature roots:

Without the feed Feature, memory reports `capabilities.changeFeed: false` and watch raises `CHANGE_ITERATOR_NOT_ASSEMBLED`. Notifications alone enable `subscribeChanges()`. The feed requires notifications; omitting them raises `CHANGE_CONTROLLER_NOT_ASSEMBLED`. A lightweight lifecycle owner still closes physical resources and drains accepted writes.

Backend authors import the controller factory from `/authoring/change-controller` and pass it explicitly to `core.createChangeController(options, createBackendChangeController)`. blocks.text: Put initial plugins in `plugins`. A later `use()` returns a host type that includes the new backends. Both references share one lifetime; close either host reference once.

Plugins in one batch cannot borrow each other's unpublished backends. Install base backends first, then install a cache, archive or other composed plugin with `use()`. IDs must be unique throughout the host.

`autoDetect` defaults to `true`. Set it to `false` when configuration must finish before checks, then explicitly call `detect()`. Concurrent checks share their Promise; successful checks are cached and failed checks can be retried. `installTimeoutMs` bounds the entire install batch in milliseconds, defaults to `30000`, and accepts finite nonnegative numbers. Failed installation rolls back that batch's resources without deleting previously installed backends.

The memory backend can write strings, bytes and records in one transaction. A failed callback does not commit its draft. Obtain queries through the `records` capability; this example reads committed data after the transaction finishes.

Memory filters records on the client. With a database backend, pushdown and transaction scope depend on that backend. Conflict handling may replay a transaction callback. Keep email, payments and other effects that cannot roll back outside it.

Strings, bytes and records have channel-conflict rules for the same logical key. Choose the appropriate write policy when replacing another channel. Do not treat these channels as unrelated key spaces. Duplicate batch-write keys reject before commit; duplicate deletion keys count once.

`/entity` provides definition, connection and basic reads/writes. Optional operations require explicit subpath units. Missing units throw `ENTITY_FEATURE_REQUIRED` with `source: @migaia/storage-host` and name the required import.

Select only required units in `features`: `entityQueryFeature()` from `/entity/query` adds query/list/stream; `entityIndexesFeature()` from `/entity/indexes` adds index declaration/planning; `entityUniqueFeature()` from `/entity/unique` adds unique commit checks; `entityMigrationFeature()` from `/entity/migration` adds version plans and persisted migration; `entityKeysetFeature()` from `/entity/keyset` admits page/after. Index-backed queries and fallback uniqueness validation also require query. Migration without indexes or unique constraints scans native records or text keys directly and needs neither query nor unique. Units never enable another unit implicitly.
The unique unit captures its own constraint projections without enabling index planning. Unique write checks alone do not require the indexes unit.
`defineEntity<T>()({...})` declares an object's primary key and indexes. `connect(store)` attaches it to a backend. This example writes first, then queries through the same definition.

The repository does not close its backend. Use `orders.in(tx)` inside a transaction; `orders.batch(...)` uses one native record transaction. Schemas and codecs perform runtime validation and conversion; TypeScript types alone do not validate external input. `fromStandardSchema` is available from the same `/entity` entry. Conversion failures retain the original error through `cause`.

Select `index` or `range` first and only once. `where`, `select`, `skip` and `limit` create new query branches. Pair custom comparators with a finite `limit`, or use `first()`. `stream()` returns a disposable iterator; use `await using` or explicit `dispose()` if stopping early. When available, `watch()` supplies invalidation notifications, not result rows or reliable replay. Transaction queries do not expose `watch()`.

Select only migration when upgrading records without indexes or unique constraints. Reading an old record upgrades the returned value; call `migrate()` to persist the new envelopes. Each memory-record batch uses the original native transaction.
Declaring unique constraints still requires the unique unit. Its fallback check also requires query; migration does not supply either unit implicitly.
Organization IDs are canonical lowercase UUIDs. Saving an organization view, including extracting one of its methods, keeps that organization fixed.

Without an `org` option, the root backend uses the zero UUID. Each memory plugin instance is independent even if namespaces match. Organization views provide business operations without installation or shutdown methods. `dropOrg()` attempts every backend; a failure does not reverse successful deletions elsewhere. Inspect the aggregate error rather than treating organization deletion as a cross-backend transaction.

A non-default organization receives the capabilities its backend actually provides. A custom capability on the root backend is not copied automatically; Feature `api` methods are routed through the organization view. Native SQL/SPARQL entry points do not support organization views; use the relevant organized data APIs.

Install the optional `@migaia/logger` peer first. `storageLogStore()` is asynchronous and accepts a host or organization view, a backend ID and a nonempty `prefix`. A plain KV object is not accepted. Append one record, then inspect its sequence and pending state:

Log records are separate from business keys. Business enumeration, clear and capacity limits do not touch them. A backend must support the required log storage; opening it first recovers confirmed state. Exclusive storage permits one open handle for an organization and prefix, while shared transactional storage may permit several. Truncation does not reuse sequence numbers. An unconfirmed write stops further operations: close and reopen the log to recover. Old log handles reject with `STORE_DISPOSED` after `dropOrg()`.

Opening a log does not enable automatic business logging. Configure `createStorageHost({ plugins: [storageJournalPlugin(), backend], journal: ... })` for that. Supply `{ logger, namespace, ... }` directly, or use an asynchronous initializer for each organization. The initializer receives `orgId` and asynchronous `storageLogStore(id, { prefix })`. The host borrows the logger and does not shut it down.

Choose binlog, WAL, undo and same-transaction log stores as needed. `atomicBinlog` / `atomicUndo` select real log stores by backend ID and require a shared transaction with the business backend. Other combinations depend on backend support and reject before business mutation when unavailable. Failed external binlog appends are reported without rolling back committed business data. Do not recover unknown results by blindly replaying writes. Undo checks stored data and revisions first; conflicts use `UNDO_CONFLICT`, and missing history uses `UNDO_NOT_FOUND`.

`telemetry: true` additionally requires the logger level plugin. Logs can include operation payloads and errors; configure the logger for the application's needs. Even telemetry-only configuration installs an asynchronous stage, so use asynchronous data methods; synchronous reads and writes reject with `ASYNC_STAGE_IN_SYNC_ENTRY`. With neither journal configuration nor a `/journal` import, the host does not load logger at runtime. See the logger guide for logger configuration.

Business failures reject the operation's Promise. Observer and reporting-callback failures do not change completed data operations. Use `report(error)` for these diagnostics and inspect `source`, `code` and the original `cause`.

symbols.purpose: The single augmentable event map shared by host construction, stage adapters and hooks.on; observers cannot veto storage.
symbols.core:
onEvict: Committed native eviction count for one channel; emitted after actual commit.
beforeHostInstall: Original initial or later install batch is about to run.
afterHostInstall: The original plugin tuple committed and became published.
onHostInstallError: The original install batch failed; payload contains its semantic failure code.
beforeBackendPluginInstall: Observe exact backend identity before its original plugin installation.
afterBackendPluginInstall: Original backend plugin preparation completed successfully.
onBackendPluginInstallError: Original backend plugin installation failed with a normalized code.
beforeHostClose: Original close begins with the current registered backend count.
afterHostClose: Original host cleanup finished; the lifecycle remains terminal.
onHostCloseError: Original host cleanup collected failures; observer only reports its code.
beforeEnvelopeCheck: Known target version before the original archive validation.
afterEnvelopeCheck: Archive validation succeeded and the stored version is now known.
onVersionRejected: The original archive version check rejected the supplied data.
beforeMigrationStep: Original ordered migration step is about to receive its input.
afterMigrationStep: Original migration step completed successfully.
afterMigrate: Original migration plan or reset completed with its actual elapsed time.
beforeEncode: Original codec is about to encode the proposed value.
afterEncode: Original codec encoding completed successfully.
onEncodeError: Original codec encoding failed with its normalized semantic code.
beforeDecode: Original codec is about to decode persisted input.
afterDecode: Original codec decoding completed successfully.
onDecodeError: Original codec decoding failed with its normalized code.
beforeQuery: Original query plan has been prepared before its native cursor opens.
afterQuery: Original query completed with actual result and execution counts.
onQueryError: Original query failed; observation reports its semantic code.
beforeTransaction: Before the original native transaction is created.
onTransactionStart: Original native transaction has been registered with its authentic id.
beforeTxOperation: Before one already-admitted authentic transaction operation.
afterTxOperation: After one original transaction operation settles.
beforeCommit: Original final-check boundary immediately before native commit.
afterCommit: Original native owner confirmed commit and actual changed-key count.
afterRollback: Original native rollback completed with its primary failure retained.
onTransactionClose: Original native transaction resource reached its actual end.
beforePersistFlush: Before the original transactional persistence flush.
afterPersistFlush: Encoding and native requests completed; this alone is not a commit certificate.
beforeBackendCreate: Before original native backend construction acquires resources.
afterBackendCreate: Original backend construction returned its actual native object.
onBackendRejected: Original runtime backend admission rejected its candidate.
afterBackendInstall: Original backend and its selected capabilities were installed.
onBackendDisposeStart: Original backend cleanup started after admission was sealed.
afterBackendDispose: Original backend cleanup reached its terminal boundary.
beforeSql: Before the actual native SQL request; only statement bytes and parameter count are observed.
afterSql: After actual native SQL execution with elapsed time and affected rows.
onSqlError: Actual native SQL execution failed; only the normalized code is exposed.
beforeStorageOperation: Before the original public endpoint’s actual work.
afterStorageOperation: The original endpoint settled successfully with actual count and elapsed time.
onStorageOperationError: Original endpoint failed and retained its primary failure.

afterLogOperation: Original durable log operation completed.
onLogOperationError: Original durable log operation failed.
beforeLogClose: Original durable log resource begins cleanup.
afterLogClose: Original durable log cleanup finished.
onLogCloseError: Original durable log resource cleanup failed.
onAppend: Original logger append published committed records.

symbols.purpose: The exact installed plugin tuple’s original registry, business access, hooks and root lifecycle.
symbols.core:
hooks: The original typed synchronous observer registry; failures only report.
extensions: Frozen installed plugin extensions; explicitly contextual methods use this fixed organization.
api: Per-backend selected Feature API, preserving original client and authentic transaction projection.
detect: Run only the registered original backend checks and await their cleanup.
Completes detection or rejects its original coded failure.
org: Return a new immutable business view under this root lifecycle, retaining exact plugin inference.
org.orgId: Caller-created canonical UUID, normally returned by createOrgId.
A fixed-org view with no installation, deletion or disposal authority.
dropOrg: Attempt every admitted backend target for this organization without closing existing business views.
dropOrg.orgId: Canonical UUID returned by createOrgId or an existing org view.
Completes all deletions; failures aggregate original errors and successful targets are not rolled back.
use: Atomically install one readonly tuple through the original PluginHost batch and rollback failed preparation.
use.plugins: Original handles returned by definePlugin or native backend plugin factories.

backend: Look up the exact original admitted backend by its installed literal id.
backend.id: Literal id returned on the originally installed plugin handle.

hasBackend: Check original published membership without preparing or opening a backend.
hasBackend.id: Candidate id chosen by the caller from installed plugin ids.

backends: Return the current readonly membership snapshot with exact admitted backend values.

dispose: Seal the original host, drain accepted work and release installed resources in their existing order.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: The exact installed plugin tuple’s original registry, business access, hooks and root lifecycle.

sections.title: 上手

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
hooks: The original typed synchronous observer registry; failures only report.
extensions: Frozen installed plugin extensions; explicitly contextual methods use this fixed organization.
api: Per-backend selected Feature API, preserving original client and authentic transaction projection.
detect: Run only the registered original backend checks and await their cleanup.
Completes detection or rejects its original coded failure.
org: Return a new immutable business view under this root lifecycle, retaining exact plugin inference.
org.orgId: Caller-created canonical UUID, normally returned by createOrgId.
A fixed-org view with no installation, deletion or disposal authority.
dropOrg: Attempt every admitted backend target for this organization without closing existing business views.
dropOrg.orgId: Canonical UUID returned by createOrgId or an existing org view.
Completes all deletions; failures aggregate original errors and successful targets are not rolled back.
use: Atomically install one readonly tuple through the original PluginHost batch and rollback failed preparation.
use.plugins: Original handles returned by definePlugin or native backend plugin factories.
The same runtime host with the widened installed tuple; await detect after later native installation. Duplicate or overlapping batches reject.
backend: Look up the exact original admitted backend by its installed literal id.
backend.id: Literal id returned on the originally installed plugin handle.
Exact native store with selected Features; org views return a close-free fixed-org borrow.
hasBackend: Check original published membership without preparing or opening a backend.
hasBackend.id: Candidate id chosen by the caller from installed plugin ids.
True narrows the id to this host’s published registry keys.
backends: Return the current readonly membership snapshot with exact admitted backend values.
Readonly map; org views project each value into the same fixed organization.
dispose: Seal the original host, drain accepted work and release installed resources in their existing order.
The original cached cleanup Promise; all failures remain inspectable through causes or aggregate errors.
codecStages: Bind report-only codec encoding and decoding to this exact store registration.
codecStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
Original observer methods; they allocate no backend, transaction or diagnostic queue.
queryStages: Bind report-only query planning and completion to this exact store registration.
queryStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
transactionStages: Bind report-only native transaction boundaries to this exact store registration.
transactionStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
concurrencyStages: Bind report-only original concurrency decisions to this exact store registration.
concurrencyStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
backendStages: Bind report-only original backend creation and disposal to this exact store registration.
backendStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
sqlStages: Bind report-only original native SQL request observations to this exact store registration.
sqlStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
operationStages: Bind report-only original storage endpoint observations to this exact store registration.
operationStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
envelopeStages: Bind report-only archive validation/migration stages to one exact store and operation.
envelopeStages.store: Exact admitted store or authenticated business borrow returned by this host.
envelopeStages.operation: Original repository operation name and target version.
Original envelope observers retaining only primitive operation context.

installTimeoutMs: Nonnegative finite millisecond budget covering the complete original install batch, including preparation.

scheduler: Borrow an IScheduler from @migaia/utils/scheduler for original deadlines and elapsed-time observations.

report: Observe the exact secondary Error or thrown value; returned thenables are observed and reporter failures are contained.

Route hook and cleanup failures to the application’s diagnostic sink.
hooks: Initial synchronous observer map, sharing the same registry as host.hooks.on; observer failures report without vetoing storage results.
Omitted: no initial observers are registered.
Observe original host or backend boundaries from the first installation.

symbols.purpose: One captured fixed-org borrowed logger configuration; selected commit recording uses the original asynchronous bootstrap stage.
symbols.core:
logger: Original Logger with actual selected durable/level plugins; storage borrows it and never shuts it down.
namespace: Caller-selected nonempty stable recovery namespace, combined with exact backend and org identity.
binlogValues: Optional true adds committed encoded values to binlog entries; omission omits those values. WAL always retains full images.
atomicBinlog: Explicit backend-id map of exact storageLogStore objects from the same registration for native log/data composition.
indexedDbUndo: Explicit true opts into the IndexedDB original undo combination; omission does not grant that capability.
atomicUndo: Exact same-registration private undo carriers selected by backend id; unrelated matching ids cannot replace them.
telemetry: Optional true requires the actual level plugin and emits ordinary storage-category entries with original payload/Error references.
redoWal: The exact shared latest-pending WAL object used by every text redo participant; same names or independent cached writers do not prove sharing.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.

symbols.core:
journalNotAssembled: Install storageJournalPlugin before journal options or private log access; no automatic runtime is loaded.
changeControllerNotAssembled: Select the backend notification Feature or supply the explicit controller factory before subscribing.
changeIteratorNotAssembled: Select memoryChangeFeedFeature and its notification producer before calling memory watch.
entityFeatureRequired: Select the entity Feature named by the message before calling its optional operation.
backendIdInvalid: Repair the plugin’s bounded ASCII id before installing.
backendDuplicate: Choose a distinct id or retry after the original batch settles.
backendNotInstalled: Install this exact id or select a currently installed backend.
backendPluginInvalid: Repair the descriptor or store that failed runtime admission.
backendInstallFailed: Inspect original creation/preparation failure; the batch remains unpublished.
storageHostBusy: Wait for the active original install batch, then explicitly retry.
storageHostDisposed: Use a new host after closure; sealed resources are not revived.
storageHostDisposeFailed: Inspect all original cleanup failures and treat the resource as terminal.
orgDeleteFailed: Every target was attempted; inspect original failures and retry without rolling back successful deletions.
backendKindMismatch: Use the authentic backend kind selected by this installed store.
invalidConfig: Repair malformed schema, codec or author configuration.
validationFailed: Inspect the original schema rejection before changing the proposed value.
serializeFailed: Encoding rejected before backend I/O; inspect the original codec cause.
deserializeFailed: Preserve stored bytes and inspect the original decoding failure.
duplicateKey: Another channel owns the key; explicit replace removes that owner.
indexUniqueConflict: Another record owns the projected unique value; repair the proposed commit.
indexBackfillFailed: Backfill and failed-readiness persistence both failed; inspect every cause.
migrationFailed: Correct the original application migration failure before retrying.
versionUnsupported: Stored data is newer than this definition; use a compatible entity version.
transactionFailed: Inspect the original memory native transaction failure.

members.name: backendIdInvalid

members.name: backendDuplicate
members.description: A backend ID is already present in the host install batch or registry. Callers must use a * distinct ID or wait for the existing batch before retrying.

members.name: backendNotInstalled
members.description: A lookup requested a valid backend ID that has not been installed. Callers must install that * exact backend or select an installed ID.

members.description: A backend plugin or store failed its runtime contract check. Callers must repair the plugin * definition rather than relying on an unvalidated store.

members.name: backendInstallFailed
members.description: Backend creation, preparation, or PluginHost installation failed. Callers may retry after * fixing the cause, while the failed batch remains unpublished.

members.name: storageHostBusy
members.description: A host mutation was requested while another install batch is active. Callers must wait for that * batch to settle and explicitly retry.

members.name: storageHostDisposed
members.description: A host or its public operation was used after sealing or terminal disposal. Callers must create * a new host instead of reviving this one.

members.name: storageHostDisposeFailed
members.description: Host cleanup collected failures or a controlled backend finalizer rejected without a semantic * identity. Callers inspect the original cleanup cause and treat that resource as terminal.

members.name: orgDeleteFailed

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Stable semantic host failure scenarios; inspect source together with a code and retain every original cause.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import StorageErrorCode from @migaia/storage-host, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.content: Use StorageErrorCode when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when StorageErrorCode does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
journalNotAssembled: Install storageJournalPlugin before journal options or private log access; no automatic runtime is loaded.
changeControllerNotAssembled: Select the backend notification Feature or supply the explicit controller factory before subscribing.
changeIteratorNotAssembled: Select memoryChangeFeedFeature and its notification producer before calling memory watch.
entityFeatureRequired: Select the entity Feature named by the message before calling its optional operation.
backendIdInvalid: Repair the plugin’s bounded ASCII id before installing.
backendDuplicate: Choose a distinct id or retry after the original batch settles.
backendNotInstalled: Install this exact id or select a currently installed backend.
backendPluginInvalid: Repair the descriptor or store that failed runtime admission.
backendInstallFailed: Inspect original creation/preparation failure; the batch remains unpublished.
storageHostBusy: Wait for the active original install batch, then explicitly retry.
storageHostDisposed: Use a new host after closure; sealed resources are not revived.
storageHostDisposeFailed: Inspect all original cleanup failures and treat the resource as terminal.
orgDeleteFailed: Every target was attempted; inspect original failures and retry without rolling back successful deletions.
backendKindMismatch: Use the authentic backend kind selected by this installed store.
invalidConfig: Repair malformed schema, codec or author configuration.
validationFailed: Inspect the original schema rejection before changing the proposed value.
serializeFailed: Encoding rejected before backend I/O; inspect the original codec cause.
deserializeFailed: Preserve stored bytes and inspect the original decoding failure.
duplicateKey: Another channel owns the key; explicit replace removes that owner.
indexUniqueConflict: Another record owns the projected unique value; repair the proposed commit.
indexBackfillFailed: Backfill and failed-readiness persistence both failed; inspect every cause.
migrationFailed: Correct the original application migration failure before retrying.
versionUnsupported: Stored data is newer than this definition; use a compatible entity version.
transactionFailed: Inspect the original memory native transaction failure.
journalRecordInvalid: Owned journal bytes are malformed; retain them and stop using the damaged payload.
journalRecoveryFailed: Recovery or commit result is uncertain; close and reopen from durable head.
undoConflict: Current full revision or value differs; no restoration was written.
undoNotFound: No committed images exist for this target and transaction id.
extensionFailed: Inspect the original callback failure retained with operation and phase.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Canonical host messages and parameterized text factories; applications branch on semantic codes rather than these diagnostic strings. The vectorMmr entry diagnoses invalid MMR lambda, topN or hit vectors from the independent scorer.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import StorageErrorText from @migaia/storage-host, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use StorageErrorText when its const contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when StorageErrorText does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained const example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

symbols.purpose: Construct the original lifecycle shell synchronously; createStorageHost is the asynchronous initial-install and detection entry.
symbols.core:
options: Captured original host lifecycle options; plugins are installed separately with use.
The original host facade, owned and closed by its caller.
hooks: The original typed synchronous observer registry; failures only report.
extensions: Frozen installed plugin extensions; explicitly contextual methods use this fixed organization.
api: Per-backend selected Feature API, preserving original client and authentic transaction projection.
detect: Run only the registered original backend checks and await their cleanup.
Completes detection or rejects its original coded failure.
org: Return a new immutable business view under this root lifecycle, retaining exact plugin inference.
org.orgId: Caller-created canonical UUID, normally returned by createOrgId.
A fixed-org view with no installation, deletion or disposal authority.
dropOrg: Attempt every admitted backend target for this organization without closing existing business views.
dropOrg.orgId: Canonical UUID returned by createOrgId or an existing org view.
Completes all deletions; failures aggregate original errors and successful targets are not rolled back.
use: Atomically install one readonly tuple through the original PluginHost batch and rollback failed preparation.
use.plugins: Original handles returned by definePlugin or native backend plugin factories.
The same runtime host with the widened installed tuple; await detect after later native installation. Duplicate or overlapping batches reject.
backend: Look up the exact original admitted backend by its installed literal id.
backend.id: Literal id returned on the originally installed plugin handle.
Exact native store with selected Features; org views return a close-free fixed-org borrow.
hasBackend: Check original published membership without preparing or opening a backend.
hasBackend.id: Candidate id chosen by the caller from installed plugin ids.
True narrows the id to this host’s published registry keys.
backends: Return the current readonly membership snapshot with exact admitted backend values.
Readonly map; org views project each value into the same fixed organization.
dispose: Seal the original host, drain accepted work and release installed resources in their existing order.
The original cached cleanup Promise; all failures remain inspectable through causes or aggregate errors.
codecStages: Bind report-only codec encoding and decoding to this exact store registration.
codecStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
Original observer methods; they allocate no backend, transaction or diagnostic queue.
queryStages: Bind report-only query planning and completion to this exact store registration.
queryStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
transactionStages: Bind report-only native transaction boundaries to this exact store registration.
transactionStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
concurrencyStages: Bind report-only original concurrency decisions to this exact store registration.
concurrencyStages.store: Exact backend returned by this host, or its authenticated fixed-org borrow.
backendStages: Bind report-only original backend creation and disposal to this exact store registration.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Construct the original lifecycle shell synchronously; createStorageHost is the asynchronous initial-install and detection entry.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import StorageHostFacade from @migaia/storage-host, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use StorageHostFacade when its class contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when StorageHostFacade does not match the required inputs or return contract.

sections.title: 快速实现
sections.content: Use a maintained class example that demonstrates real inputs and observable behavior.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
options: Captured original host lifecycle options; plugins are installed separately with use.
The original host facade, owned and closed by its caller.
hooks: The original typed synchronous observer registry; failures only report.
extensions: Frozen installed plugin extensions; explicitly contextual methods use this fixed organization.
api: Per-backend selected Feature API, preserving original client and authentic transaction projection.
detect: Run only the registered original backend checks and await their cleanup.
Completes detection or rejects its original coded failure.
org: Return a new immutable business view under this root lifecycle, retaining exact plugin inference.
org.orgId: Caller-created canonical UUID, normally returned by createOrgId.
A fixed-org view with no installation, deletion or disposal authority.
dropOrg: Attempt every admitted backend target for this organization without closing existing business views.
dropOrg.orgId: Canonical UUID returned by createOrgId or an existing org view.
Completes all deletions; failures aggregate original errors and successful targets are not rolled back.
use: Atomically install one readonly tuple through the original PluginHost batch and rollback failed preparation.
use.plugins: Original handles returned by definePlugin or native backend plugin factories.
The same runtime host with the widened installed tuple; await detect after later native installation. Duplicate or overlapping batches reject.
backend: Look up the exact original admitted backend by its installed literal id.
backend.id: Literal id returned on the originally installed plugin handle.
Exact native store with selected Features; org views return a close-free fixed-org borrow.
hasBackend: Check original published membership without preparing or opening a backend.
hasBackend.id: Candidate id chosen by the caller from installed plugin ids.
True narrows the id to this host’s published registry keys.
backends: Return the current readonly membership snapshot with exact admitted backend values.
Readonly map; org views project each value into the same fixed organization.
dispose: Seal the original host, drain accepted work and release installed resources in their existing order.
The original cached cleanup Promise; all failures remain inspectable through causes or aggregate errors.

options: Original assertLive/closingSignal/report, native facts, reservation, authenticated private transaction and native transaction entry.
Promise of IStorageJournalNamespace. run and terminal subscriptions retain accepted work until actual onEnd; transactionInfo is a pure authenticated fact. No raw client, installer or backend close rights.
assertLive: Synchronous original backend admission check; a throw prevents namespace construction or subsequent private work.
Normal return permits work; the original coded admission error is thrown synchronously.
Keep namespace access within the native backend admission boundary.
closingSignal: Original backend closure signal initiating namespace release while accepted native work drains.
report: Receives asynchronous cleanup failures from closure or symbolic disposal without replacing a primary result.
report.error: Original asynchronous cleanup cause supplied by the namespace resource owner.
The original diagnostic observer receives the failure; no native retry or replacement commit is started.
Preserve cleanup diagnostics separately from an original primary transaction failure.
backend: Original backend diagnostic kind attached to namespace admission and disposal errors.
undefined; errors omit a backend-specific diagnostic value.
nativeAtomic: Backend fact about all-or-nothing native transaction semantics; resource reservation alone cannot grant atomic rollback.
The original native transaction supplies all-or-nothing mutation and rollback.
The native owner does not guarantee all-or-nothing rollback; WAL, undo and atomic-store combinations stay unsupported.
Declare the existing native guarantee accurately before selecting atomic journal combinations.
indexExclusive: Explicit false means logger indexes must reload from the native transaction each operation; it does not weaken or strengthen nativeAtomic.
Omitted retains the exclusive namespace index contract of the original backend.
Restore the current logger index inside each original native transaction; never retain it across operations.
Use false when independent handles share the physical namespace and no lifetime-exclusive index can be retained.
reserve: Original physical owner invokes hold after reservation is acquired and awaits it until release; acquisition rejection rejects namespace creation.
reserve.hold: Async callback invoked once the original reservation is acquired; its settlement releases that reservation.
Original reservation Promise, rejecting on native acquisition or retained-work failure.
Connect the private namespace lifetime to the existing physical owner reservation.
authenticate: Synchronously validate the exact live original scope and return its existing transaction identity and private journal port; foreign scopes reject.
authenticate.scope: Exact backend-issued original live transaction scope, without capability lookup authority.
The original transaction info and journal port; foreign or expired scopes throw before private I/O.
Borrow journal work from an already admitted authentic native transaction.
transaction: Run the callback on the original newly admitted native transaction port and settle only after the native owner settles; never create a second commit owner.
transaction.work: Async callback receiving the original native journal transaction port; callback rejection stays with its native owner.
Callback value only after original native transaction settlement; unknown outcomes remain failures.
Start one original native transaction when no caller transaction scope is supplied.

declaredConfiguration.description: Optional iterator page-size hint: an integer from 1 through 4096. No default is inserted here.

declaredConfiguration.name: orgId
declaredConfiguration.description: Optional canonical lowercase UUID supplied by an outer host. The contract preserves omission; the host chooses the default organization and owns namespace mapping.

symbols.purpose: Run the sole logical policy loop while awaiting every accepted native attempt through cleanup.

Optional execute(captured, invokeOriginalLoop) wraps the real native loop once so before-next, after-next and catch remain in the original pipeline and call budget. Optional executeAttempt(captured, proceed), mutually exclusive with execute, wraps each native commit attempt: acquisition retries stay within one stage; a fully unwound commit conflict rethrows its exact coded identity before the original policy can retry. Promise of the awaited committed value. Conflict errors preserve backend cause; cancellation awaits real attempt termination. Exact nested attempt contexts reuse the original budget and retain captured backend extension fields.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
source: IRecordQuerySource captures pushdown facts, execute and optional readonly asyncDisposeKey once. execute receives only safe-prefix conditions, optional fields and captured operation context; projected native rows are unknown. Pass the host's existing resource key when it supplies a fallback for native Symbol.asyncDispose.
methods: Optional Feature-owned pure method object; capture once and retain each function reference on every where/select/requirePushdown result.
IRecordQuery<T,TContext,TAugmentMethods> with three where forms, one select, all, real stream, explain, requirePushdown, limit and orderByComparator(compare).limit(k). Missing comparator bounds and invalid limits reject before source execution. Selector ordering, distinct and skip share the same reader. Extended native controls require explicit nativeSteps:true; legacy limit/comparator behavior stays client-side. all synchronously admits its full mapper/cleanup lifetime to the original transaction iterator owner and retains its first failure before cleanup.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
generation: Index generation issued by ensureRecordIndexes and retained by this session.
ownerToken: Lease token issued by the native openBackfillSession call and retained for heartbeat/commit checks.
renew: Renew the original native lease without replacing its owner identity.
renew.ctx: Optional IOperationContext supplied by the entity call or native author. Its signal and deadline stay with the original backend operation.
Settles after native heartbeat persistence; stale ownership or cancellation rejects.
readBatch: Read the next bounded native page and optionally await entity preparation outside the IDB transaction.
readBatch.ctx: Optional IOperationContext supplied by the entity call or native author. Its signal and deadline stay with the original backend operation.
readBatch.options: Optional original prepare callback; omitted returns candidates without preparations.
Original phase/checkpoint/endOfScan plus candidate rows and optional aligned preparations; this read does not commit projections.
commitBatch: Atomically recheck the issued batch, current lease and candidate revisions before writing projections and checkpoint.
commitBatch.batch: Prepared IRecordIndexBackfillBatch from this session’s matching read; preserve its identity facts.
commitBatch.ctx: Optional IOperationContext supplied by the entity call or native author. Its signal and deadline stay with the original backend operation.
Native readiness after confirmed commit; stale rows, foreign ownership or invalid batches reject without claiming completion.
fail: Persist failure of the current native backfill generation through its original owner.
fail.cause: Original preparation or commit error, passed unchanged for native failure persistence.
fail.ctx: Optional IOperationContext supplied by the entity call or native author. Its signal and deadline stay with the original backend operation.
Settles after the native failure record; the caller must retain a persistence rejection alongside its original cause.
release: Immediately invalidate this borrowed session’s local authority; pending work remains in the original backend lifetime.
No result; the original backend retains persistent lease expiry and native resource ownership.

query: Create an immutable entity query over the connected store and materialization pipeline.

put: Validate, normalize and encode one domain value before committing its entity envelope.
put.value: Caller domain object containing the configured primary-key property.
put.ctx: Optional caller operation context and original concurrency policy; no new transaction owner or retry loop is created.

remove: Delete this entity identity through the original backend and its unique-index projection rules.
remove.id: Application entity identifier from its configured primary-key field, or the logical key returned by repository.put().
remove.ctx: Optional caller operation context and original concurrency policy; no new transaction owner or retry loop is created.
A promise resolving after deletion completes; no logical delete count is returned.
list: Collect materialized entity rows using the selected source, invalid-row policy and bounded ordering.
list.options: Caller list or indexed-list options; range, index, direction, invalid-row policy and comparator/limit correlation select the source and result.
list.ctx: Optional caller operation context with signal, timeoutMs and pageSize; an original transaction scope inherits its context instead.
Domain rows in final query order after the original reader has closed.
stream: Iterate materialized entity rows with the original query cursor and operation resource ownership.

stream.ctx: Optional caller operation context with signal, timeoutMs and pageSize; an original transaction scope inherits its context instead.

findBy.ctx: Optional caller operation context with signal, timeoutMs and pageSize; an original transaction scope inherits its context instead.

symbols.purpose: Factory options for the independent pure MMR scorer; the helper never retrieves vectors or truncates the query result itself.
symbols.core:
lambda: Finite relevance weight in [0,1]. One uses engine relevance alone; zero uses diversity after the first engine candidate, with ties retaining engine order.
topN: Positive safe integer bounding the greedy prefix, capped by the actual hit count. Remaining candidates receive ranks in engine order, so the returned score array always matches the input length.
Omitted: compute the greedy order for all hits. Actual truncation belongs only to rerank options.topN.
parameters: This type declaration has no parameters.
